buildLead: I plan to prepare ready-made kits so you will not have to spend several days checking whether a particular water meter works with Autolejek. A ready-made solution will not always be suitable, however, and sometimes an installation has to be built from scratch. This chapter will help you choose the right components and find a solution that fits your needs. You do not have to read everything from beginning to end. Paste a link to this page into an AI tool and ask a specific question, such as: ‘Will the AB-32 water meter work with Autolejek?’

installationFullPipeTitle: Keep the pipe completely filled with water
installationFullPipeText: During measurement, the water meter and the pipe section containing it should be completely filled with water. Arrange the installation so that no air pocket remains at the measurement point.
installationFullPipeAlt: Left: a pipe completely filled with water and a green check mark. Right: a partially filled pipe with an air gap and a red cross.
installationFullPipeCaption: Correct: water fills the entire pipe cross-section. Incorrect: an air gap remains above the water.
installationIntro: This section brings the previously selected components together. Start by tracing the water path: identify the source, pump or control valve, meter and outlet. Then consider what happens to water and air during filling, dosing and stopping.
installationLayoutText: For a system with a pump and a dosing valve, a starting layout is: source → pump → inlet pipe section → meter → outlet pipe section → dosing valve → destination. With mains water, omit the pump; when dosing is controlled by the pump alone, a dosing valve may be unnecessary. This is a conceptual layout; select filters, check valves and service fittings for the actual equipment.
installationSpacingText: Always determine pipe section lengths and dimensions from the documentation for the water meter, solenoid valves and all other devices in the system. Check the required straight sections upstream and downstream of each device and the permitted mounting orientations. Account for these requirements around elbows, filters and valves too. The illustrations below are conceptual and do not specify installation distances.
installationLowCaption: The meter sits at the bottom of a U-shaped section. The downstream pipe rises again, helping retain water. This illustrates the principle; determine straight pipe lengths separately.
installationLowAlt: A meter at the bottom of a U-shaped pipe; water flows down on the left, through the meter and up on the right.
installationHighTitle: Incorrect: the highest point of the pipe
installationHighCaption: Air can collect in the upper section. Flowing water does not mean the meter cross-section is completely filled.
installationHighAlt: A meter at the top of an inverted U, with an air gap above the water in the horizontal pipe.
installationOutletTitle: Incorrect: a descending pipe with a free outlet
installationOutletCaption: An open outlet below the meter allows the measuring section to drain. Flow in this layout does not ensure a full pipe.
installationOutletAlt: A partially filled pipe containing a meter leads to a downward elbow and an open outlet.
installationAssemblyOne: Before assembly, check component flow arrows, connection compatibility and access for disconnection and cleaning. Leave room to remove the meter without dismantling the entire installation.
installationAssemblyTwo: Support and align the pipes without stress. The meter must not carry the pipework; do not pull misaligned pipes together using flange bolts.
installationAssemblyThree: Before the first dose, fill the installation and remove air. Check joints for leaks and confirm that water actually stops reaching the destination when the pump stops or the valve closes.
installationAssemblyFour: Connect the pulse output according to the selected meter manual and set the pulse conversion in Autolejek. Test against a measured volume and check how the system behaves after restarting.
installationReferenceText: The B METERS MAG manual recommends placing the meter downstream of the pump and valves downstream of the meter. It covers electromagnetic meters: always check grounding, connections, straight pipe lengths and electrical outputs for your own model.
installationReferenceLink: B METERS MAG — manual, chapters 4–6 (PDF, EN)
installationValveTitle: Solenoid valve downstream of the flow meter
installationValveText: The solenoid valve is usually installed downstream of the flow meter, in the direction of water flow. Maintain the distances and mounting orientations required by the documentation for both devices.
installationValveCaption: Example layout: the flow meter sits in a lowered pipe section, followed by the solenoid valve in the direction of flow. Determine pipe section lengths from the equipment documentation.
installationValveAlt: A U-shaped pipe with a flow meter at the bottom and a solenoid valve on the downstream section to the right; arrows show flow from the meter to the valve.
installationManualValveTitle: A simple way to reduce excessive flow
installationManualValveText: If the flow rate is too high, you can add a manual valve and partially close it to reduce the amount of water passing through per unit of time. This is an inexpensive, practical way to match the flow to your installation. In the illustrated layout, the manual valve is downstream of both the flow meter and the solenoid valve: you set the flow manually, while the solenoid valve still starts and stops dosing automatically.
installationManualValveSelection: Choose a valve approved by its manufacturer for flow regulation while partially open. Adjust it gradually while monitoring flow and staying within the operating ranges of the pump, flow meter and solenoid valve. Check their documentation for the required spacing between components.
installationManualValveCaption: Example order: flow meter → solenoid valve → manual valve for reducing flow. The illustration shows component placement, not the required spacing or the handle position for regulation.
installationManualValveAlt: A flow meter at the bottom of a U-shaped pipe, followed by a solenoid valve and a manual valve with a red handle. Arrows indicate the direction of flow.
